prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Interactive Desktop Pet Controls Walkthrough [finish, redesign]: predicted +7.0%, measured -31.0% (p=0.00028), stopped early: finish worse
- round 1: Defer Sign-In After Pet Selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +8.0%, measured -0.1% (p=0.960261), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Setup Time Estimate on Story Screen [choose_path, copy]: predicted +3.0%, measured -0.3% (p=0.899652), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Interactive Tips During Generation Wait [home, wait_info]: predicted +6.0%, measured -1.2% (p=0.671809), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Pet Customization Photo Upload Guidance Redesign [adoption, redesign]: predicted +3.0%, measured +0.2% (p=0.960906), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Simplified Desktop First Spawn Welcome Screen [finish, redesign]: predicted -5.0%, measured +6.3% (p=0.24065), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Account Sign-In Session Reassurance [sign_in, hint]: predicted +2.0%, measured -5.4% (p=0.029985), lost: worse
- round 2: Path Selection Choice Cards Layout [choose_path, layout]: predicted +0.5%, measured +5.9% (p=0.001625), won

Previous lessons:
Interactive walkthrough redesigns on the finish stage significantly hurt completion rates.
Reordering steps (like deferring sign-in) had no clear effect on conversion.
Adding copy estimates and wait-time info showed no clear effect.
Predictions were consistently too high across all test types, anticipating positive gains where results were neutral or negative.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Layout changes to choice cards were helpful and significantly improved conversion.
Interactive walkthrough redesigns on the finish stage and sign-in reassurance hints significantly hurt conversion.
Reordering steps, adding copy estimates, wait-time info, and photo upload guidance showed no clear effect.
Predictions were consistently too high for walkthroughs, hints, reordering, and copy changes, anticipating positive gains where results were neutral or negative.
Predictions were too low for layout changes, underestimating the actual positive impact.
